- predictable tail latency at p95 for short-chat style prompts (~50-150 tokens)
- a clear autoscale strategy for our batch scoring jobs (embeddings + rerankers) that run every 15 minutes

Subject: Re: Post-call: workload sample + a few clarifying items

Hi Samantha — great to meet you both earlier. Appreciate the sample. High-level recap and proposed next steps below so we start the technical session with concrete targets.

Quick recap of what we heard:
- Primary priority: consistent p95 latency for user-facing chat (short prompts).
- Secondary: scheduled batch scoring (embeddings -> reranker -> store) with predictable throughput.
- Constraints: mixed runtime stack (Go + Python), VPC requirement for data in prod.

Immediate asks (we'll cover in the tech deep-dive):
- SDK/auth: we support REST + official SDKs (Python, Node, Go community client). We recommend server-side tokens for batch workers + mTLS for private deployment.
- Routing: set policy per-route (latency-first for chat; cost-first for batch) with automatic fallback to smaller variants.
- Structured output/tool calling: we have function-calling patterns and schema validation examples — will share a snippet and validation harness.
- Embeddings/rerankers: recommended batch sizes, shard strategy, and how to route short vs long queries into different queues.

For dedicated capacity sizing, please confirm whether the csv rows represent concurrent workers or sequential single-worker events. Ben/ Karthik — I asked for a quick initial capacity sketch we can bring to the call.

Next steps:
1) Ben to share a preliminary capacity/queueing recommendation doc.
2) Karthik to outline telemetry + tracing headers we need to surface in our instrumentation.
3) Set technical deep-dive for 60–75 minutes (suggest Wed/Thu next week).

I'll attach our SDK quickstart and a short structured-output example to the calendar invite for the deep-dive.

Best,
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Integration & capacity follow-up: traffic shaping, queues, and SDK/auth next steps

Samantha — adding some concrete guidance ahead of the deep-dive so the call can focus on numbers and tradeoffs. High level recommendations (for Dedicated capacity):

1) Latency-sensitive chat (user-facing)
- Target: p95 < 300ms for 50–150 token responses.
- Concurrency guidance: reserve 12–16 concurrent request slots per A100-equivalent GPU for chat-optimized variants (quantized float16/8 pipelines).
- Queues: dedicated low-latency queue with aggressive preemptive batching disabled; small dynamic batch window (10–20ms) to preserve tail latency.

2) Batch scoring (embeddings + reranker)
- Throughput target: support 20k embeddings/min peak across scheduled jobs.
- Batch sizes: embeddings: 128–1024 depending on embedding length; reranker: prefer micro-batching of 16–64 for pairwise scores.
- Autoscale policy: scale out on queue-depth / 60s rolling throughput with a 2-minute cooldown. Warmup: keep 1 hot node per pool for <30s cold start SLA.

3) Concurrency limits + traffic shaping
- Per-customer per-route concurrency: enforce soft limit (e.g., 200 concurrent requests) with a token-bucket for bursts and a hard limit per-pool.
- Fallbacks: route to quantized variants when headroom < 20% or to hosted pool (lower-cost but higher latency) during outages.

4) Auth/SDK notes
- Use server-side scoped API keys for production; short-lived mTLS certs for private deployments.
- For Go backend, our community Go client + direct REST is production-tested; provide snippet.

I've attached a short capacity sketch (pdf) with baseline cluster sizing for a 3x redundancy SLA. We'll refine after we see the full workload distribution.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Inference
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_capacity_estimate_q1.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: Integration & capacity follow-up: traffic shaping, queues, and SDK/auth next steps

Thanks all — quick instrumentation and ops notes to add:

- Telemetry: sample at request-level + token-level cost summary in traces. Surface a per-request model_id and kernel_variant tag.
- Tracing headers: inject X-Redwood-Req-ID and propagate through batch workers so reranker logs can be correlated to upstream chat events.
- Alerts: p95 latency > 350ms, queue depth > 75% sustained for 2 minutes, embedding batch error rate > 1% should trigger a P1.
- Rate limiting: recommend per-route rate limits with separate buckets for interactive vs batch; interactive gets a smaller, prioritized bucket.

We'll bring a sample tracing/profiling dashboard to the call — can be shared ahead if you want to review.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Architect
Redwood Inference
